localChanges: chore: update civ1-world, civ2-world, civ1-unit and civ2-unit (#1346)

log: `sleepAboardWith(ruleRegistry, turn, unitRegistry)` makes a `Stowed` effect whose `Sleep` uses the game's own registries, and `lifecycleRules` registers it with its own (and a new optional `turn`), so the unit's `Sleeping` looks for enemies in the game's unit registry rather than core-unit's instance (civ-clone/web-renderer#1110). `sleepAboard(unit)` is unchanged. base-unit-action-sleep is now ^0.1.5, the first with `Sleep`'s `unitRegistry`.

`StartWorldOptions` takes an optional `landMassRegistry`, passed to `World`, so a game built with its own registries finds its continents in `game.landMasses` rather than core-world's instance (civ-clone/web-renderer#301).

The sleep action and the stowed rule pass the game's unit registry (and the stowed rule its rule registry and turn) to `Sleep`, so in a game built with its own registries a sleeping unit wakes when an enemy comes beside it (civ-clone/web-renderer#1110).

The start rule passes `game.landMasses` to `startWorld`, so a game built with its own registries finds its continents where it looks (civ-clone/web-renderer#301). Its unused `generatorRegistry` argument is dropped.

The sleep action passes the game's unit registry to `Sleep`, and the lifecycle rules get the game's turn, so the stowed rule's `Sleep` uses the game's own registries too: in a game built with its own registries a sleeping unit wakes when an enemy comes beside it (civ-clone/web-renderer#1110).
The start rule passes `game.landMasses` to `startWorld`, so a game built with its own registries finds its continents where it looks (civ-clone/web-renderer#301).
